    AI Overview
    The Artemis I Orion spacecraft splashed down in the Pacific Ocean on December 11, 2022, west of Baja California near Guadalupe Island. The capsule touched down at 9:40 a.m. PST, concluding a 25.5-day mission around the Moon. 
    Key details of the splashdown: 
    • Location: Pacific Ocean, west of Baja California.
    • Date: December 11, 2022.
    • Time: 9:40 a.m. PST (12:40 p.m. EST).
    • Mission Goal: Final testing of the heat shield, which handled temperatures of nearly 5,000 degrees Fahrenheit. 
    Following the splashdown, the USS Portland retrieved the capsule to conclude the maiden flight of the Artemis program.

    When did Artemis 1 splashdown?
    December 11
    Reentry and splashdown

    The spacecraft separated from its service module at around 17:00 UTC on December 11 and then reentered Earth's atmosphere at 17:20 UTC travelling near 40,000 km/h (25,000 mph).
